\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مسافرخانه} (mosâferkhâne)}{مسافرخانه (mosâferkhâne)}]{\fa{مسافرخانه} (mosâferkhâne) — a guesthouse, a cheap inn}

\label{lesson:FA-C437-mosaferkhane}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a dhow, then the Persian for to drop anchor.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مسافرخانه}}
\textbf{\fa{مسافرخانه}} (\emph{mosâferkhâne}) — \textquotedblleft{}a guesthouse, a cheap inn\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{شب} \fa{در} \fa{یک} \fa{مسافرخانه} \fa{ارزان} \fa{ماندیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Shab dar yek mosâferkhâne-ye arzân mândim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We spent the night in a cheap guesthouse.
\end{quote}

\emph{mosâfer} 'traveller' + \emph{khâne} 'house'. Simpler and cheaper than a \emph{hotel}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{mosâferkhâne} is built from \emph{mosâfer} 'traveller', borrowed from Arabic \emph{musāfir}, and native \emph{khâne} 'house', usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{xānag}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mosâferkhâne}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mosâferkhâne}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{mosâferkhâne}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a dhow, then the Persian for to drop anchor, then say \emph{mosâferkhâne} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اقامتگاه} (eqâmatgâh)}{اقامتگاه (eqâmatgâh)}]{\fa{اقامتگاه} (eqâmatgâh) — lodgings, a place to stay; a residence}

\label{lesson:FA-C437-eqamatgah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to drop anchor, then the Persian for a guesthouse.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اقامتگاه}}
\textbf{\fa{اقامتگاه}} (\emph{eqâmatgâh}) — \textquotedblleft{}lodgings, a place to stay; a residence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{اقامتگاه} \fa{ما} \fa{نزدیک} \fa{دریا} \fa{بود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Eqâmatgâh-e mâ nazdik-e daryâ bud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our lodgings were near the sea.
\end{quote}

\emph{Eqâmatgâh-e bumgardi} — a guesthouse in a village home, now common in the countryside.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{eqâmatgâh} is built from \emph{eqâmat} 'a stay', a loan usually traced to Arabic \emph{iqāma} 'staying, residing', and native \emph{gâh} 'place'. EtymDB does not list it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to drop anchor, then the Persian for a guesthouse, then say \emph{eqâmatgâh} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پانسیون} (pânsiyon)}{پانسیون (pânsiyon)}]{\fa{پانسیون} (pânsiyon) — a boarding house; full board}

\label{lesson:FA-C437-pansiyon}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a guesthouse, then the Persian for lodgings.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پانسیون}}
\textbf{\fa{پانسیون}} (\emph{pânsiyon}) — \textquotedblleft{}a boarding house; full board\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دانشجوها} \fa{در} \fa{یک} \fa{پانسیون} \fa{زندگی} \fa{میکنند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dâneshju-hâ dar yek pânsiyon zendegi mikonand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The students live in a boarding house.
\end{quote}

Also meals included with a room: \emph{bâ pânsiyon} — with full board.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pânsiyon} was borrowed from French and is usually traced to French \emph{pension} 'board and lodging'. EtymDB does not list the Persian word.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سوئیت} (su'it)}{سوئیت (su'it)}]{\fa{سوئیت} (su'it) — a suite; a small self-contained flat}

\label{lesson:FA-C437-suit}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for lodgings, then the Persian for a boarding house.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سوئیت}}
\textbf{\fa{سوئیت}} (\emph{su'it}) — \textquotedblleft{}a suite; a small self-contained flat\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{شمال} \fa{یک} \fa{سوئیت} \fa{کوچک} \fa{اجاره} \fa{کردیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar shomâl yek su'it-e kuchek ejâre kardim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the north we rented a small flat.
\end{quote}

At the seaside in Iran a \emph{su'it} is often a one-room holiday flat with a kitchen.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{su'it} was borrowed from a European language and is usually traced to French \emph{suite} 'a set of rooms'. EtymDB does not list the Persian word.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اقامت} \fa{کردن} (eqâmat kardan)}{اقامت کردن (eqâmat kardan)}]{\fa{اقامت} \fa{کردن} (eqâmat kardan) — to stay (somewhere), to reside}

\label{lesson:FA-C437-eqamat-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a boarding house, then the Persian for a suite.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اقامت} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{اقامت} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{eqâmat kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to stay (somewhere), to reside\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{سه} \fa{شب} \fa{در} \fa{این} \fa{هتل} \fa{اقامت} \fa{کردیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Se shab dar in hotel eqâmat kardim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We stayed three nights in this hotel.
\end{quote}

\emph{eqâmat} 'stay' + \emph{kardan}: more formal than \emph{mândan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{eqâmat kardan} is built from \emph{eqâmat} 'a stay', a loan usually traced to Arabic \emph{iqāma} 'staying, residing', and \emph{kardan} 'to do', inherited from Middle Persian \emph{kardan} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
